analysis.title: US Credit Alpha: Down but not out
key_insights: Credit spreads widened with the risk-asset sell-off. IG and HY cash widened 5bp and 22bp as of Wednesday's close, leaving both within 2bp of year-to-date wides. Barclays calls it a correction, not a collapse.
AI-related IG names widened 6bp on the week. Basic industries also lagged in IG (+6bp) and HY (+28bp) as commodity prices fell. IG natural gas and energy also underperformed.

CDX.IG was 2bp wider and CDX.HY 14bp wider, so derivatives outperformed cash. CDX.HY continued to decompress versus CDX.IG, partly because of widening in stressed and distressed constituents since the roll.
IG supply stayed heavy. $31bn priced through Wednesday, taking November to $150bn, the highest November on record.

10y real rates were nearly unchanged at 2.88% after rising 28bp the prior week. Hike expectations pushed real yields higher, but credit has looked through the move. The risk is that real rates rise enough to tighten financial conditions materially, with the weakest balance sheets most exposed.

Barclays expects IG spreads to trade sideways to tighter into year-end as seasonal supply slows, with dispersion staying elevated. It favors carry and longer spread duration in IG, remains negative on cyclicals, and is neutral on quality in HY while avoiding the most distressed names.
2027 US fixed income net supply (ex-bills) is forecast at $3.07trn, down 4% from 2026. Lower Treasury and securitized supply offsets higher corporate issuance, and munis stay near record levels.

Treasury net note and bond issuance is forecast to fall to $1.03trn from $1.19trn as bills absorb more financing. 10y-equivalent supply falls about 20%, from $781bn to $620bn. Coupon increases start at the August 2027 refunding, concentrated through 10y with 20y and 30y unchanged. Bills rise to 25% of marketable debt.
Treasury raised the maximum size of long-end buybacks from $2bn to $6bn, with eight operations per quarter. That removes about $32bn per quarter that private investors must absorb.

Corporate supply is forecast at $2.97trn gross and $1.37trn net in 2027. IG is a record $2.1trn gross (+11%), HY $380-420bn (+13%), and broadly syndicated loans $450-490bn (+7%). AI financing drives IG, increasingly outside the index through chip, data center and neocloud deals.
IG issuance is expected to skew shorter. 10y+ supply grows 5% to $360bn, versus +13% in 1-5y. Banks add about $295bn and utilities about $170bn.

Securitized net issuance is forecast to fall 22% to $426bn, with gross down 14% to $2.1trn. Higher rates suppress refinancing and housing turnover, and Basel III endgame leads banks to retain loans. Muni supply stays near record levels and the market could approach $5trn by year-end 2027.

IG sector spread dispersion rose 29% from its September 8 trough of 0.26 to 0.33 on November 16, above the long-term average of 0.30. AI-issuer spread standard deviation rose from 24bp to 67bp over the past year.

AI's weight in IG is rising. Hyperscalers' share of DTS doubled from 4.8% to 9.6%, and the AI ecosystem's DTS share rose from 7.8% to 14.1%. AA spreads are 66bp, versus 49bp excluding AI, which compresses the AA/A differential to 7bp.

Barclays likes BBBs in the belly of the curve after recent decompression. The BBB/A ratio rose from 1.50 in September to 1.58. Ex-AI ratios at the 3y and 30y tenors sit at the 24th and 15th percentiles of their five-year ranges.

IG upgrades: BDCs and media entertainment to Overweight, and life insurance, retailers and food to Market Weight. Downgrades: cable satellite to Market Weight, and healthcare, refining, chemicals, tobacco, restaurants, supermarkets, wireless and wirelines to Underweight.

BDC upgrade rationale: spreads near +190bp with OAD under 3 let the sector widen 66bp and still match IG on excess returns. Fundamentals are deteriorating, with non-accruals rising and negative net flows. About 20% of holdings are software borrowers, which is the AI-disruption risk.
Retailers are held back by AMZN, about 40% of the sector. Barclays sees room for AMZN to issue by 1Q27 against an estimated $110bn funding need, $80bn of it in USD.
Media upgrade: META is about 48% of the index and is adding equity alongside debt. SKYD is 17% of the sector and the main downside risk, but its first-lien notes are near the wides.

Technology stays Underweight. Wide spreads have not produced better excess returns, and chip financing is increasing competition for capital. ORCL is positively viewed, but it is only 11.5% of the sector.

HY sector changes: upgrade Other REITs to MW and Wirelines to OW. Downgrade FinCos, Healthcare Products, Independent Energy, OFS, Packaging and Semis to UW, and Hardware, Leisure, Retailers, Tech Services and Wireless to MW.

HY concentration matters. XRX is 81% of Hardware OAS (594bp headline, 115bp ex-XRX) and HTZ is 52% of Transportation Services OAS. Cable satellite is the largest contributor to HY OAS, and removing it would tighten the index 12bp.
Rate-vol sensitivity in HY is highest for airlines, aerospace/defense, construction machinery, home construction and autos. Barclays notes it is in the middle of a hiking cycle.

Leveraged loans: the Performing LLI returned 3.7% YTD versus 0.4% for HY and -1.9% for IG, but price is about 2pts lower. Hotels/Restaurants/Leisure, Professional Services and Trading Companies screen attractive. Aerospace & Defense, Electrical Equipment, Machinery and Pharmaceuticals screen rich.

Software loans: Barclays favors straddling BBs and higher-quality single-Bs. Software rated BB+ to B-flat trades at $96.1 and a 495bp 3y DM, and the recompression of single-Bs versus BBs looks overdone.

CMBS: 23 loans totaling over $4bn have exposure to Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros Discovery. Management targets at least $6bn of run-rate synergies, including at least $2.2bn from overhead, real estate and facilities. Key New York exposures are 30 Hudson Yards, 1515 Broadway and 230 Park Avenue South.

earnings_insights: Barclays says aggregate Q3 results for the largest regional gaming operators (CZR, MGM, PENN, BYD, CHDN) showed revenue +2% and EBITDA +0%.
Barclays says Q3 lodging data show RevPAR growth averaging about 7.0% y/y across HLT, H, MAR, RHP, SVC and WH.
Barclays says companies in aerospace & defense have generally exceeded earnings expectations and raised guidance since coverage began.
Barclays says SKYD's management targeted at least $6bn of annualized run-rate synergies within three years in its November 9 earnings update.

AI capex slowing, and heavy AI-related supply creating a supply premium and volatility in IG credit.
Record IG supply is a technical headwind in 2027.
Spectrum auctions in 1H27 may re-lever the Big 3 telcos.

Thursday's session saw early strength reverse into a sharp midday sell-off that left equities and CDX at their lows and wides.
About 8% of HY index CUSIPs had a move greater than 5pts this year, versus just under 12% on average since 2010 excluding 2020.
geopolitical: The war in Iran kept oil prices higher, supporting independent energy and midstream returns.
Barclays cites dual geopolitical shocks in the Middle East and Russia that produced windfall refining margins.
Midterm elections shifted control of the House and Senate to Democrats, which Barclays says affects regulatory risk for tobacco, finance companies and healthcare.

tension_points.bull_case: Barclays macro strategists say the cycle remains intact, with strong earnings, resilient global growth and a resilient US consumer. IG spreads should trade sideways to tighter into year-end as supply slows.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher real rates could tighten financial conditions materially, with the weakest balance sheets most exposed. AI capex concerns and record supply persist.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Real rates rising far enough to tighten financial conditions materially.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand for AI continues to outstrip supply, so a collapse in capex looks unlikely.
tension_points.bear_case: Heavy hyperscaler, chip and data center financing creates a supply premium and volatility, and competition for capital may widen spreads further.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Growing chip financing supply competing for capital, which would weigh further on tech spreads.
